lessons.title: 写一封提醒，需要把全部联系人交出去吗？
lessons.content:
# 写一封提醒，需要把全部联系人交出去吗？

## 一份草稿，先用公开材料就能开始

你准备把[NASA的2023年观月活动公告](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/)改写成一段发给朋友的历史活动介绍。公告已有时间、地点和参加方式；你的手机里另外保存着朋友的姓名和联系方式。现在只需要写文字，还不发送。

## 先猜一下

现在只写这段历史活动介绍，你会先给助手哪些材料，哪些暂时不需要提供？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

不需要。先提供公开公告和读者的角色，就能练习表达；真实的收件人资料，留到真要处理收件人时再考虑。

## 按当前动作选材料，不按工具能拿多少选

你可以这样请求：“根据这则2023年的公开公告，写一段给朋友的历史活动介绍，保留时间和地点，不发送。”这里不需要朋友的邮箱，也不需要其他联系人的信息。

[ChatGPT agent在2025年的发布说明](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/)提醒用户，任务不需要的连接可以关闭。它记录了一种控制思路，而不是承诺所有助手都会自动替你收窄范围。

:::detail[不提供姓名，会不会写得不够像我？]
先看姓名对当前修改有没有作用。你要试着把通知写得亲切，可以用“写给熟悉这项活动的朋友”来说明关系，不必提供真实邮箱和手机号码。你要检查姓名拼写，才需要那一个具体名字。把“听起来像给朋友写的”与“能够把信送到这个人手里”分开，就能少提供很多无关信息。不是所有私人材料都永远不能使用，而是每次提供前知道它具体服务哪项动作。
:::

根据当前任务，决定先使用公开材料，还是检查经过授权的具体名单。这里不会读取联系人或发送消息。

::play{#minimum-personal-data-weigh}

## 什么时候该反过来

任务真的变成核对一份已经获准使用的收件人名单时，名单才成为必要材料。仍然只处理相关那部分，不把“需要几个收件人”扩大成“可以读取所有联系人”。

:::detail[用角色替换姓名，就等于完全匿名了吗？]
不能这样保证。内容里可能还保留地点、具体经历或其他能让人认出对象的信息。这里做的是减少与任务无关的资料，不是给一份文件颁发匿名证明。你可以先通读准备提供的文字：这项细节会影响语气、事实核对或成品结构吗？不会，就先去掉。会影响，也应想清楚你是否有权把它交给这个工具。公开公告加上自己原创的请求，是一个无需私人材料也能练习的起点。
:::

:::detail[怎样给一次协作写出清楚边界？]
把允许的动作与材料放在同一句要求里，例如“只根据这段公开公告写草稿，不读取通讯录，不发送”。这些话能讲清意图，但代替不了工具真正的权限设置。能查看权限时，再检查是否开了不需要的连接。完成后你得到的是草稿，不是已经寄出的消息；下一步是否添加收件人、是否发送，需要另作决定。这样你并没有牺牲写作帮助，只是把不同责任放回了不同步骤。
:::

:::detail[怎样确认删掉的资料确实无关？]
用剩下的材料再读一次你的要求：是否仍然知道公告讲什么、写给哪类读者、最后交什么？这些已经足够时，就可以先写。要是真缺了哪项事实，先记下来待补，不必把整个私人文件夹都交出去。
:::

## 自检

你只想把一封自己写的邮件改得更礼貌。把真实邮箱改成“同事”、删去无关电话，会妨碍哪一项修改？哪项需要保留的信息又应先确认使用权？

## 一句话

**材料和权限跟着当前任务走，不因为工具能读取更多就提供更多。**

en.title: Do You Need to Hand Over All Your Contacts to Write a Reminder?
en.content:
# Do You Need to Hand Over All Your Contacts to Write a Reminder?

## A Draft Can Start with Public Materials Alone

You are planning to adapt [NASA's 2023 Moon observation event announcement](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/) into a historical event intro to send to friends. The announcement already includes the time, location, and how to participate; your phone separately stores your friends' names and contact details. Right now, you only need to write the text, not send it yet.

## Predict first
If you are only writing this historical event introduction right now, which materials would you give the assistant first, and which do you not need to provide for now?

Write down your judgment first, then read on for the answer.

## Answer
You do not need to. Providing the public announcement and the readers' role first is enough to practice phrasing; save actual recipient details for when you truly need to handle recipients.

## Choose Materials by the Current Action, Not by How Much the Tool Can Take

You can prompt it like this: "Based on this 2023 public announcement, write a historical event introduction for friends, keeping the time and location, without sending it." Here, there is no need for your friends' email addresses, nor any information about other contacts.

[ChatGPT agent's 2025 release notes](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/) remind users that connections not needed for a task can be turned off. It documents a way of thinking about control, rather than promising that all assistants will automatically narrow the scope for you.

:::detail[If I don't provide names, will it not sound enough like me?]
First check whether names serve any purpose for the current revision. If you want to try making the notice sound warm and friendly, you can describe the relationship with "written for friends familiar with this event," without providing real email addresses or phone numbers. Only when you need to verify name spelling do you need that specific name. Separating "sounding like it was written for a friend" from "being able to deliver the letter into this person's hands" allows you to leave out a lot of irrelevant information. It is not that private materials can never be used at all, but that before providing them each time, you know specifically which action they serve.
:::

Decide whether to use public materials first or check an authorized specific list based on the current task. Contacts will not be read, and messages will not be sent here.

::play{#minimum-personal-data-weigh}

## When to choose the other way

Only when the task truly turns into checking an approved recipient list does that list become necessary material. Even then, still process only the relevant portion, without expanding "needing a few recipients" into "allowing access to all contacts."

:::detail[Does replacing names with roles equal complete anonymity?]
No such guarantee can be made. The content may still retain locations, specific experiences, or other information that could identify the subject. What we are doing here is reducing information irrelevant to the task, not issuing a certificate of anonymity for a document. You can first read through the text you intend to provide: will this detail affect tone, fact-checking, or the structure of the final piece? If not, remove it first. If it does, you should also think carefully about whether you have the right to hand it over to this tool. A public announcement combined with your own original request provides a starting point to practice without requiring any private materials.
:::

:::detail[How do you set clear boundaries for a collaboration?]
Put permitted actions and materials in the same instruction sentence, such as: "Draft based only on this public announcement, do not access contacts, and do not send." These words clarify intent, but they cannot replace a tool's actual permission settings. When you can review permissions, check again whether unnecessary connections are enabled. When finished, what you get is a draft, not a sent message; whether to add recipients or send in the next step requires a separate decision. In this way, you do not sacrifice writing assistance; you simply place different responsibilities back into different steps.
:::

:::detail[How do you confirm that removed details are truly irrelevant?]
Re-read your prompt using only the remaining materials: do you still know what the announcement is about, what kind of audience it is written for, and what needs to be delivered in the end? When those are already sufficient, you can go ahead and write. If a specific fact is genuinely missing, note it down to fill in later, without needing to hand over your entire private folder.
:::

## Check yourself
You only want to polish an email you wrote to make it more polite. Which revision would be hindered by changing real email addresses to "colleague" and deleting irrelevant phone numbers? And which information that needs to be kept should have its usage rights confirmed first?

## In one sentence
**Materials and permissions follow the current task; do not provide more just because a tool can access more.**

lessons.title: 看到“临时”两个字，可以不看设置了吗？
lessons.content:
# 看到“临时”两个字，可以不看设置了吗？

## 一个名字相同的功能，也有不同选项

[ChatGPT的临时聊天帮助页](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8914046)区分个性化与非个性化两种临时聊天，并分别说明历史、已有记忆和新记忆。你准备先选一种方式，再开始处理一段公开文字。

## 先猜一下

你这次只想依据刚提供的公开文字作答，不带过去的偏好。开始前会检查哪种控制，为什么？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

应检查是否启用了个性化。所查帮助页说明，个性化临时聊天可以使用已有偏好，非个性化选项不使用记忆、自定义指令和插件。

## 把几个控制项分别读一遍

不新增记忆、是否使用已有记忆、是否出现在历史中，并不是同一个问题。页面还说明：临时聊天若被主动保存，会变成普通聊天，随后按账户相应设置处理。

你可以先写一句自己要的边界：“这次不参考我已有的偏好。”再找对应控制项，而不是用功能名称代替阅读。

:::detail[为什么“不新增”与“不使用已有的”要分开？]
先分清两个动作：是从记录里读信息，还是往里写新内容。一个设置可以允许前者但禁止后者。帮助页正是这样区分个性化临时聊天的：它可以参考已有记忆，但在保持临时状态时不创建或更新记忆。你要的是不带旧背景，就应当检查读取已有内容的选项，不能只看有没有新增。这个区分也能帮助你读懂其他工具的设置说明，而不必背住一个永久不变的按钮位置。
:::

:::detail[选错之后，可以在同一段对话中途切换吗？]
本次查阅的帮助说明要求在开始时选择是否个性化，开始后不能在这段临时聊天里更换这项选择。因此，处理材料之前先看一眼设置，比已经提供材料以后再猜更有用。若产品将来调整功能，回到当前说明核对即可。你不需要凭记忆坚持旧步骤。要紧的是先表达自己的目标，再确认工具实际提供的控制是否与目标对应。仅在对话里写一句要求，并不等于已经改变了产品的账户设置。
:::

:::detail[临时记录不在历史中，就表示没有任何保留吗？]
界面上不显示，并不等于所有系统里真的没有数据。帮助页还列出安全保留与第三方动作的边界；发送给第三方的资料受接收方规则约束。你现在不必记住所有保留期限，但应知道遇到敏感材料时要找哪部分说明：历史显示、个性化、模型改进、保留与外部接收方。课程里的公开材料让你能够先学会阅读这些区别，而不必拿私人数据试错。
:::

把每个问题放到它真正询问的控制范围。不要用同一个“临时”标签回答所有问题。

::play{#temporary-does-not-mean-nothing-sort}

## 自检

关闭一项用于模型改进的选项，是否就能断定旧文件与聊天历史都被删掉了？你会把这个问题拆成哪几个具体控制？

## 一句话

**先看一个设置控制哪个动作，再判断它是否符合你的需要。**

en.title: When You See the Word "Temporary", Can You Skip the Settings?
en.content:
# When You See the Word "Temporary", Can You Skip the Settings?

## A Feature with the Same Name Can Still Have Different Options

The [ChatGPT temporary chat help page](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/8914046) distinguishes between personalized and non-personalized temporary chats, explaining history, existing memories, and new memories separately. You plan to choose one mode before you begin working with a piece of public text.

## Predict first
This time, you only want answers based on the public text you just provided, without bringing in past preferences. Before starting, which control would you check, and why?

Write down your reasoning first, then read on for the answer.

## Answer
You should check whether personalization is enabled. The help page consulted explains that personalized temporary chats can use existing preferences, while non-personalized options do not use memories, custom instructions, or plugins.

## Read Each Control One by One

Not adding new memories, whether existing memories are used, and whether a conversation appears in history are not the same question. The page also explains that if a temporary chat is explicitly saved, it turns into a regular chat and is then handled according to the account's corresponding settings.

You can start by writing down the boundary you want: "Do not reference my existing preferences this time." Then look for the corresponding control, rather than letting a feature name replace reading the documentation.

:::detail[Why separate "not adding new" from "not using existing"?]
First distinguish between two actions: reading information from records, or writing new content into them. A setting can allow the former while forbidding the latter. This is exactly how the help page distinguishes personalized temporary chats: they can reference existing memories, but do not create or update memories while remaining temporary. If what you want is not to carry over old context, you should check the option for reading existing content, rather than only looking at whether new memories are added. This distinction also helps you understand settings descriptions in other tools, without having to memorize a permanently fixed button location.
:::

:::detail[Can you switch midway through the same conversation if you made the wrong choice?]
The help documentation consulted requires choosing whether to personalize at the start; once started, you cannot change this choice within that temporary chat. Therefore, glancing at the settings before processing materials is more useful than guessing after you have already provided them. If the product changes features in the future, simply return to the current documentation to verify. You do not need to rely on memory to stick to old steps. What matters is first stating your goal, then confirming whether the controls the tool actually provides match that goal. Simply writing a request inside the chat does not mean you have changed the product's account settings.
:::

:::detail[Does a temporary record not being in the history mean nothing is retained at all?]
Not displaying on the interface does not mean there is truly no data anywhere across all systems. The help page also lists the boundaries of safety retention and third-party actions; materials sent to third parties are subject to the recipient's rules. lessons.title: 对话不见了，上传的文件也一定不见了吗？
lessons.content:
# 对话不见了，上传的文件也一定不见了吗？

## 对话与材料，可能放在不同地方

[ChatGPT文件存储与资料库说明](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001052)介绍了可再次使用的上传文件。页面把删除聊天与删除已保存文件分别说明。你不想再用某份旧材料，准备先整理自己的资料。

## 先猜一下

删除相关对话以后，还需要检查哪个地方，才能知道这份旧材料是否仍在？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

还要检查资料库中的文件。所查说明明确区分聊天与已保存文件，删除聊天不会自动删除资料库里保存的那份文件。

## 结束一次对话

对话记录的是这次交流。文件则可能被保存下来供下一次选择。你可以结束交流，但那不等于同时管理了所有可复用材料。

:::detail[为什么要把它们分开管理？]
资料复用意味着同一个文件可能服务不止一次对话。你下次不必重新上传，这很方便；也正因为它有独立用途，清理一次聊天就不必然清理这份材料。这里不推测软件内部怎样存储，只按帮助页明确说明的用户可见行为判断。整理时可以列两个目标：哪些交流记录不再需要，哪些文件不应继续保留或复用。把两件事分开处理，才不会以为按一个按钮就都处理好了。
:::

这两列按帮助页说明比较管理范围，不是实际执行删除。关注“资料库主列表中有没有该文件”，而不是宣称所有系统永久清除。

::play{#chat-and-file-are-different-contrast}

## 管理仍可复用的材料

先查看文件究竟在资料库，还是连接着外部存储的原件。所查说明还指出，连接的Google Drive文件仍由其原服务管理，不能把ChatGPT中的操作当作已经删除原件。

:::detail[从列表里消失，是否等于所有地方立刻永久删除？]
不能这样推断。帮助页把主列表、可能存在的最近删除区及永久删除安排分别说明，也列出相应例外。你要做的是按当前产品提供的路径确认状态，而不是根据界面少了一行就向别人保证“所有副本都没有了”。下载到自己的电脑、发给别人的文件或存放在外部服务的原件，也不是同一个列表能代为证明的。把对象说清楚，会比只用“删了”两个字更准确。
:::

:::detail[只是下次不使用它，也一定要删除文件吗？]
不一定。你可以先从新任务选用的材料里移开它；删除是另一项管理决定。保留有用的旧材料没有问题，但要防止它在不相关的新任务中被误当成依据。例如你已经从旧年份的公告切换到另一个年份，就先核对当前选中的资料。别为了整理材料，顺手把还要保留的原件给删了。这里的练习只判断范围，不会替你执行任何删除。
:::

## 自检

你只是希望下一次整理新公告时不再使用旧文件，应该先检查当前选用材料，还是直接承诺原文件已经永久删除？为什么？

## 一句话

**先确认资料在哪里，再选择管理动作；删除聊天不等于删除所有相关材料。**

en.title: If a Chat Is Gone, Is the Uploaded File Definitely Gone Too?
en.content:
# If a Chat Is Gone, Is the Uploaded File Definitely Gone Too?

## Chats and Materials May Be Kept in Different Places

The [ChatGPT file storage and library documentation](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001052) introduces reusable uploaded files. The page explains deleting chats and deleting saved files separately. You no longer want to use a certain piece of old material, and prepare to organize your materials first.

## Predict first
After deleting the relevant chat, which other place do you still need to check to know whether this old material is still there?

Write down your judgment first before looking down at the answer.

## Answer
You also need to check files in the library. The documentation examined clearly distinguishes chats from saved files; deleting a chat does not automatically delete the file saved in the library.

## Ending a Conversation

A chat records this specific exchange. Files, on the other hand, may be saved for you to choose next time. You can end an exchange, but that does not equal managing all reusable materials at the same time.

:::detail[Why manage them separately?]
Material reuse means that the same file can serve more than one conversation. You do not have to upload it again next time, which is convenient; precisely because it has an independent purpose, cleaning up a chat does not necessarily clean up this material. We do not speculate here about how the software stores things internally, but judge only by the user-visible behavior explicitly described on the help page. When organizing, you can list two goals: which conversation records are no longer needed, and which files should not be kept or reused any longer. Handling the two things separately prevents you from assuming that clicking one button takes care of everything.
:::

These two columns compare management scopes according to the help page instructions, rather than actually performing a deletion. Focus on "whether the file is in the main library list," instead of claiming permanent removal across all systems.

::play{#chat-and-file-are-different-contrast}

## Managing Materials That Can Still Be Reused

First check whether the file is actually in the library or is an original connected to external storage. The documentation examined also points out that connected Google Drive files are still managed by their original service, and actions in ChatGPT cannot be treated as having deleted the original file.

:::detail[Does disappearing from the list equal immediate, permanent deletion everywhere?]
You cannot deduce that. The help page explains the main list, any recently deleted section that might exist, and permanent deletion schedules separately, while also listing corresponding exceptions. What you need to do is confirm the status according to the path provided by the current product, rather than promising others that "all copies are gone" just because a line disappeared from the interface. Files downloaded to your own computer, files sent to others, or originals stored on external services cannot be proven on their behalf by this same list either. Stating the specific object clearly is more accurate than simply using the words "it's deleted."
:::

:::detail[If you simply won't use it next time, must you delete the file?]
Not necessarily. You can first remove it from the materials selected for the new task; deletion is a separate management decision. There is nothing wrong with keeping useful old materials, but you need to prevent them from being mistakenly used as references in unrelated new tasks. For example, if you have already switched from announcements of an older year to another year, check the currently selected materials first. Do not accidentally delete the original you still want to keep just for the sake of organizing materials. The exercises here only evaluate scope and will not perform any deletion for you.
:::

## Check yourself
If you simply want to stop using the old file the next time you organize new announcements, should you first check the currently selected materials, or directly promise that the original file has been permanently deleted? Why?

## In one sentence
**Confirm where the materials are first, then choose management actions; deleting a chat does not equal deleting all related materials.**

lessons.title: AI 写得很顺，能直接发吗？
lessons.content:
# AI 写得很顺，能直接发吗？

OpenAI（一家做 AI 的公司）提过一种能替人上网办事的 AI。它不只会写字，到了重要一步会停下来请人确认。这提醒你：写好一段话，不等于已经发出去。今天咱们只练前一步：先看清草稿，再决定要不要发。

你手里有张通知，自己也有事要说，想让 AI 帮着写得清楚又得体。

可话写得顺，不等于日期、名字和要求都对。今天先练一件真会遇到的事：看清草稿里的事实，再定要不要发。

::play{#draft-is-not-send-primm}

下次让 AI 帮着写要发的消息，先让它按你给的事实写一版。仔细核对日期、名字、要求和多出来的承诺，再定要不要发。

[OpenAI（做 AI 的公司）关于重要一步先让人确认的说明](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/)

en.title: The AI wrote it smoothly—can you send it right away?
en.content:
# The AI wrote it smoothly—can you send it right away?

OpenAI (a company that makes AI) has mentioned an AI that can handle online tasks for people. It doesn't just write text; when it reaches an important step, it pauses to ask a person to confirm. This is a reminder: writing a draft is not the same as sending it out. Today, we'll practice just the first step: check the draft clearly first, then decide whether to send it.

You have a notice in hand and something of your own to say, and you want the AI to help write it clearly and politely.

Even when words read smoothly, that does not mean the dates, names, and requests are correct. Today, let's practice something you might truly run into: check the facts in the draft before deciding whether to send it.

::play{#draft-is-not-send-primm}

Next time you ask the AI to help write a message to send, have it write a draft based strictly on the facts you provided. Carefully check the dates, names, requests, and any extra promises before deciding whether to send it.

[A note from OpenAI (the company that makes AI) about letting a person confirm important steps first](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/)

en.title: Write a message to the seller that you can check
en.prompt:
You bought a small bookshelf online, and after unboxing it, you found a cracked board. You'd like the AI to help write a message to the seller, explaining the situation and suggesting how to resolve it.
Write a message to the seller based on the order record, checking the facts and requests before deciding whether to send it.
rubric: Both the prompt and the drafted message focus on the new situation of the damaged bookshelf, without copying over content from the parent-teacher conference
The drafted message keeps the key facts from the record: item, order number, delivery date, damage location, and approximate length
The drafted message clearly asks for a replacement, refund, or other solution, without treating details filled in by the AI as facts
The drafted message can be reviewed before sending, and does not claim that the seller has already been contacted
请求和写好的消息都针对书架坏了这件新事，没照搬家长会内容
写好的消息保留了记录里的关键事实：商品、订单号、收货日期、损坏位置和大致长度
写好的消息说清了想换货、退款或别的处理，没把 AI 补出来的话当成事实
写好的消息发前能检查，没说已经联系过卖家

activities.brief: 可话写得顺，不等于日期、名字和要求都对。今天先练一件真会遇到的事：看清草稿里的事实，再定要不要发。

strings.AI 写得很顺，能直接发吗？: The AI wrote it smoothly—can you send it right away?
strings.OpenAI（做 AI 的公司）关于重要一步先让人确认的说明: A note from OpenAI (the company that makes AI) about letting a person confirm important steps first
strings.这里讲有些 AI 替人办事，到重要一步会先让人确认。写好草稿和发给别人不是一回事: This explains that when some AI tools take care of tasks for people, they pause at important steps to let a person confirm first. Having a draft ready and actually sending it to someone are two different things.
strings.你手里有张通知，自己也有事要说，想让 AI 帮着写得清楚又得体。: You have a notice in hand and something of your own to say, and you want the AI to help write it clearly and politely.
strings.可话写得顺，不等于日期、名字和要求都对。今天先练一件真会遇到的事：看清草稿里的事: Even when words read smoothly, that does not mean the dates, names, and requests are correct. Today, let's practice something you might truly run into: check the facts in the draft before deciding whether to send it.
strings.OpenAI（一家做 AI 的公司）提过一种能替人上网办事的 AI。它不只会写字: OpenAI (a company that makes AI) has mentioned an AI that can handle online tasks for people. It doesn't just write text; when it reaches an important step, it pauses to ask a person to confirm. This is a reminder: writing a draft is not the same as sending it out. Today, we'll practice just the first step: check the draft clearly first, then decide whether to send it.
strings.先看草稿，再决定要不要发（课内说明）: Check the draft first before deciding whether to send it (lesson note)
strings.网购书架到货损坏记录（练习）: Record of damaged bookshelf received from online shopping (practice)
strings.这是学校发来的家长会通知。我下周三出差，参加不了。帮我给班主任写条消息，说我来不: Here is a parent-teacher conference notice sent by the school. I will be on a business trip next Wednesday and cannot attend. Please help me write a message to the homeroom teacher saying I cannot make it, and that I would like to schedule another time to hear how my child has been doing lately.
strings.把通知和自己的情况交给 AI 后，最该留心哪种情况？: After giving the notice and your situation to the AI, what should you watch out for most?
strings.AI 可能把话写得很顺，却把日期、称呼或要求的轻重写偏: The AI may write very smoothly, but get the date, how you address someone, or the tone of your request wrong
strings.通知写得很清楚，AI 不会添上我没说过的内容: The notice is written clearly, so the AI will not add anything I didn't say
strings.AI 只会改改错字，不会改变我想说的意思: The AI will only fix typos and won't change what I mean to say
strings.草稿里先看什么？: What should you check first in the draft?
strings.先看 AI 有没有把意思写准，特别是日期、称呼和说话语气。: Check first whether the AI got your meaning right, especially dates, how people are addressed, and the tone of voice.
strings.把这张通知放进对话: Add this notice to the conversation
strings.你刚才猜的是：AI 可能把话写顺，却把意思写偏，或加上没说过的内容。现在拿草稿跟: What you guessed just now was: the AI may write smoothly, but get the meaning wrong or add things you never said. Now compare the draft with the notice and your original words. If it used dates from the notice, that does not mean it made things up, but make sure it is for this specific conference. If it added names or promises nobody ever mentioned, do not treat them as facts yet. Then check whether your reason for traveling and your request to reschedule were written too forcefully.
strings.草稿里的每句话，都有依据吗？: Does every sentence in the draft have a basis?
strings.刚才看过了草稿。现在只查跟请假有关的几件事，拿它跟通知和原话对一对，看每一项有没: You've looked over the draft. Now check only the few details related to asking for time off. Compare the draft with the notice and your original words to see whether each item keeps its original meaning.
strings.刚才查的不是整张通知，而是消息真用得上的信息：哪场家长会、什么时候开、你想了解什: What you checked just now was not the whole notice, but the details the message actually needs: which parent-teacher conference, when it takes place, and what you would like to know. You don't need to copy the location and every single schedule detail into the message. Then look back at your reason for the business trip and your request to reschedule, to make sure that is truly what you want to say.
strings.AI 加了一句我没说过的客气话，要留着吗？: The AI added a polite line I never said—should I keep it?
strings.先问自己是不是真想这么说。只要不是你的意思，就删掉或改掉。客气代替不了事实。: First ask yourself if you truly want to say that. As long as it isn't what you meant, delete or change it. Politeness is no substitute for facts.
strings.通知没写班主任名字，能让 AI 猜吗？: The notice didn't list the homeroom teacher's name—can I let the AI guess it?
strings.别让 AI 猜。可以先写“老师您好”，或者查到名字再填。拿不准时，留空也比编一个: Don't let the AI guess. You can start with "Hello, Teacher" or fill it in once you find the name. When you aren't sure, leaving it blank is better than making up a name.
strings.看上面的草稿，只查这条消息真用得上的信息。先看草稿有没有保住每一项，再看通知原文: Look at the draft above and check only the information this message actually needs. First check whether the draft kept each item, then check the original notice.
strings.这条消息说的是哪场家长会？: Which parent-teacher conference is this message talking about?
strings.得让老师知道你说的是哪场会，不必把地点和所有安排都抄进消息。: The teacher needs to know which meeting you're talking about, without having to copy the location and all the arrangements into the message.
strings.本学期期中家长会定于10月15日（周三）下午2:30，在各班教室举行。: This semester's midterm parent-teacher conference is scheduled for October 15 (Wednesday) at 2:30 PM, held in each classroom.
strings.日期和时间对上了，老师才知道你哪一次来不了。: When the date and time match, the teacher will know which meeting you cannot attend.
strings.你想另约时间了解什么？: What would you like to schedule another time to discuss?
strings.孩子近期的学习情况: My child's recent progress in school
strings.这正是你想另约时间的目的。写清楚，老师才知道你想了解什么。: That is the exact purpose of scheduling another time. If you write it clearly, the teacher will know what you want to learn about.
strings.怎样让草稿少替你猜？: How can you get the draft to do less guessing for you?
strings.刚才查了消息真正需要的内容。现在回到原先的请求，添一句提醒，告诉 AI 哪些话能: You've just checked the content the message actually needs. Now go back to your original request and add a reminder, telling the AI what it can write directly and what parts to leave for you to confirm. Once added, compare the two drafts side by side.
strings.让新草稿只写有依据的事实，没写明的姓名、时间和安排，留给你来定。: Have the new draft include only backed-up facts, leaving unstated names, times, and arrangements for you to decide.
strings.现在把两版草稿放在一起，看加了提醒后有没有变化。日期、称呼和安排要是来自通知或你: Now put the two drafts side by side to see if adding the reminder made a difference. If dates, how people are addressed, and arrangements come from the notice or your own words, you can keep them; if there is no basis for them, delete them or mark them first. If the AI still adds unsupported claims, that is an issue with the draft, not because you failed to ask. Even if the two drafts look similar, you still need to check them yourself, because making a request does not mean the AI has checked the facts for you. In the end, whether to send it is up to you.
strings.把下面的短句加进原请求，也能换成你自己的话。改好后重新跑一次，再把新旧草稿比一比: Add the short phrases below to your original request, or put them in your own words. After updating, run it again and compare the new and old drafts.
strings.只用通知和我刚才说过的事实: Only use facts from the notice and what I just said
strings.没写明的姓名或时间先标出来: Mark any unstated names or times first
strings.别替我加上没说过的安排: Don't add any plans I haven't mentioned
strings.先写一版短消息留给我核对: Write a short version first for me to check
strings.书架坏了，怎么写给卖家？: The bookshelf is damaged—how do you write to the seller?
strings.你在网上买了小书架，拆箱后发现有块板裂了。想让 AI 帮着写条消息发给卖家，说清: You bought a small bookshelf online, and after unboxing it, you found a cracked board. You'd like the AI to help write a message to the seller, explaining the situation and suggesting how to resolve it.
strings.照着订单记录写一条发给卖家的消息，先核对事实和要求，再决定发不发。: Write a message to the seller based on the order record, checking the facts and requests before deciding whether to send it.
strings.你想让卖家先知道什么？希望怎么处理？哪些话要留给自己确认？: What do you want the seller to know first? How would you like it handled? Which parts should be left for you to confirm?
strings.消息讲清了书架、订单或收货信息，还有第二层隔板坏在哪里: The message clearly states the bookshelf, order or delivery information, and where the second shelf board is damaged
strings.消息提出了换货、退款或别的清楚处理要求: The message makes a clear request for a replacement, a refund, or another solution
strings.消息保住材料里的关键事实，没添未给的名字、时间、原因或赔偿承诺: The message keeps the key facts from the materials without adding unprovided names, times, reasons, or promises of compensation
strings.写好的消息发之前能逐项核对，发不发依然由你来定: The drafted message can be checked item by item before sending, and whether to send it is still entirely up to you
strings.下次怎么开口？: How should you ask next time?
strings.下次让 AI 帮着写要发的消息，先让它按你给的事实写一版。仔细核对日期、名字、要: Next time you ask the AI to help write a message to send, have it write a draft based strictly on the facts you provided. Carefully check the dates, names, requests, and any extra promises before deciding whether to send it.
strings.OpenAI（一家做人工智能产品的公司）在 2025 年介绍过一种会替人上网办事: In 2025, OpenAI (a company that makes artificial intelligence products) introduced an AI that can browse the web and get things done on people's behalf. It does more than just write. When it reaches an important step, it pauses first to ask a person for confirmation. Users can also interrupt it or take over themselves. This example shows that writing a good passage and doing something on someone's behalf are not the same thing.
strings.各位家长：\n\n本学期期中家长会定于10月15日（周三）下午2:30，在各班教:

investigate.title: 草稿里的每句话，都有依据吗？

investigate.explanation: 刚才查的不是整张通知，而是消息真用得上的信息：哪场家长会、什么时候开、你想了解什么。地点和全部安排，不用全抄进消息里。再回头看看自己的出差原因和另约请求，确认那确实是你想说的话。

more.question: AI 加了一句我没说过的客气话，要留着吗？
more.answer: 先问自己是不是真想这么说。只要不是你的意思，就删掉或改掉。客气代替不了事实。

more.question: 通知没写班主任名字，能让 AI 猜吗？
more.answer: 别让 AI 猜。可以先写“老师您好”，或者查到名字再填。拿不准时，留空也比编一个名字好。

modify.title: 怎样让草稿少替你猜？
modify.brief: 刚才查了消息真正需要的内容。现在回到原先的请求，添一句提醒，告诉 AI 哪些话能直接写，哪些地方要留给你确认。加上之后，再把两版草稿放在一起比比看。

lessons.title: 长任务还在继续，你该在哪一步停下来？
lessons.content:
# 长任务还在继续，你该在哪一步停下来？

## 一项任务不只有写出文字

[ChatGPT agent在2025年的发布说明](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/)介绍了把查询与执行动作接在一起的任务，也介绍了中断与接管。你准备让助手整理一段资料，再把成稿提交到外部服务。现在文字还在修改，接下来的动作还没发生。

## 先猜一下

要在还有选择时检查成稿、接收对象和提交范围，你会把停下来的位置安排在哪里？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

安排在实际提交之前，并要求明确等待你的确认。暂停以后先看哪些步骤已完成、哪些尚未执行，再决定继续还是更改任务。

## 暂停以后，先分清已经发生与尚未发生

写出草稿、确认成稿、提交到外部服务是不同步骤。你可以明确要求：“先完成草稿，列出准备提交的内容与接收对象，等我确认再继续。”

若中途停下，先查看当前状态，不要直接重做整条任务。你要确认的是下一步还能不能改，不光看屏幕停没停滚动。

:::detail[为什么暂停后还要看已完成的步骤？]
暂停是从当前时刻介入，不是让之前的动作自动消失。先看草稿是否写好、有没有已经提交的记录，再决定后面的操作。若草稿已完成而提交未开始，你仍可以换一个读者或修改措辞；若服务已收到提交，则要到那个服务查看处理状态。直接重跑整项任务可能重复做已经完成的部分。这得看实际记录做到了哪步，不能靠“应该还没做”去猜；助手无法确认时，应把那一步保留为状态未知。
:::

:::detail[为什么不能只说“有问题就停”？]
这句话没有说明你认为哪种问题重要。对你的任务，接收对象、准备发送的具体内容、是否公开可能都值得确认。把确认点写成一个具体动作之前的要求，会让你更容易看到应该审查什么。2025年的官方介绍描述了这类人工控制，但并不证明今天任何工具都提供相同界面。开始实际使用前应核对所用工具当前的停止与确认方式；没有这类控制，就先让它只交草稿，由你自己决定下一步。
:::

:::detail[恢复编辑器里的旧稿，为什么还要另外查提交记录？]
[Canvas的发布介绍](https://openai.com/index/introducing-canvas/)描述的是文稿版本的比较与恢复。把文字恢复成旧版，并不代表外部服务也撤回了收到的内容。两个动作作用于不同对象：一个是手里的文稿，一个是外部已经处理的请求。因此，暂停后发现文字需要恢复，可以先恢复草稿；若已有对外提交，则另查相关服务提供的更正或取消方式。不要因为草稿现在正确，就把之前的发送记成从未发生。
:::

把任务状态放到对应处理栏。这里整理的是动作记录，不会替你向任何外部服务提交。

::play{#pause-before-action-sort}

## 自检

任务暂停后，你看到草稿已完成，但提交结果显示未知。为什么不能把整条流程都写成未开始？你会先核对哪一步？

## 一句话

**在重要动作前保留确认点，暂停后按已知状态决定下一步。**

en.title: When a Long Task Is Still Running, at Which Step Should You Pause?
en.content:
# When a Long Task Is Still Running, at Which Step Should You Pause?

## A Task Involves More Than Just Writing Text

[The 2025 release notes for ChatGPT agent](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-agent/) introduced tasks that chain queries and execution actions together, as well as interruption and takeover. You plan to have the assistant organize some materials and then submit the final draft to an external service. Right now, the text is still being revised, and the subsequent actions have not happened yet.

## Predict first
To check the final draft, recipient, and submission scope while you still have choices, where would you place the pause point?

Write down your judgment first, then scroll down to see the answer.

## Answer
Place it right before the actual submission, with an explicit requirement to wait for your confirmation. After pausing, check which steps have been completed and which have not yet been executed before deciding whether to continue or modify the task.

## After Pausing, First Distinguish Between What Has Happened and What Has Not

Writing a draft, confirming the final text, and submitting to an external service are distinct steps. You can explicitly specify: "Complete the draft first, list the content to be submitted and the recipient, and wait for my confirmation before continuing."

If things stop halfway through, check the current status first instead of redoing the entire task right away. What you need to confirm is whether the next step can still be modified, not just whether the screen has stopped scrolling.

:::detail[Why do you still need to check completed steps after pausing?]
Pausing intervenes from the current moment; it does not make previous actions automatically disappear. First check whether the draft is ready and whether any submission records exist before deciding on subsequent actions. If the draft is complete and submission has not started, you can still change the recipient or modify the phrasing; if the service has already received the submission, you need to check the processing status in that service. Rerunning the entire task directly might duplicate parts that have already been completed. This depends on what the actual records show has been done, rather than guessing that "it probably hasn't been done yet"; when the assistant cannot confirm, that step should remain as an unknown status.
:::

:::detail[Why shouldn't you just say "stop if there is a problem"?]
This phrasing does not specify which kinds of problems you consider important. For your task, the recipient, the specific content to be sent, and whether it is public may all be worth verifying. Writing the confirmation point as a requirement before a specific action makes it easier for you to see what should be reviewed. The 2025 official introduction described this type of human control, but that does not prove every tool today provides the same interface. Before actual use, you should verify the current stopping and confirmation mechanisms of the tool you are using; if no such controls exist, have it only deliver a draft first, and decide the next step yourself.
:::

:::detail[Why do you still need to check submission records separately when restoring an older draft in an editor?]
[The Canvas release announcement](https://openai.com/index/introducing-canvas/) describes comparing and restoring document versions. Restoring text to an older version does not mean the external service also retracted the content it received. The two actions act on different targets: one is the manuscript in hand, and the other is an externally processed request. Therefore, if you pause and find that the text needs to be restored, you can restore the draft first; if an external submission has already been made, look up the correction or cancellation methods provided by the relevant service separately. Do not treat a past sending as having never occurred just because the draft is now correct.
:::

Place each task status into its corresponding handling column. This organizes action records and will not submit anything to external services on your behalf.

::play{#pause-before-action-sort}

## Check yourself
After the task is paused, you see that the draft is completed, but the submission result shows unknown. Why can't you mark the entire workflow as not started? Which step would you verify first?

## In one sentence
**Reserve a confirmation point before important actions, and decide the next step based on known status after pausing.**

lessons.title: 熟悉的声音，下一步该联系谁？
lessons.content:
# 熟悉的声音，下一步该联系谁？

## 一条来自真实监管提醒的问题

[美国联邦贸易委员会在2024年的提醒](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2024/04/fighting-back-against-harmful-voice-cloning)讨论了仿声被用于亲人紧急求助或上司请求的风险，并给出了核实建议。听见熟悉的声音后，下一步采用哪条联系渠道，正是这份建议要解决的问题。

## 先猜一下

你会从哪里取得下一次联系的号码，怎样避免只靠同一个待核实的人证明自己？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

使用自己原先已确认的联系方式去核实，不只依赖来电者提供的新信息。声音像谁，与独立确认确实联系到了谁，是不同判断。

## 沿着对方新给的信息继续走

对方在可疑来电中提供一个号码，你再拨它，只能证明你联系到了那个号码背后的人。这本身算不上独立的身份依据。

:::detail[为什么不先考考对方，说一件只有亲人知道的事？]
这里采用FTC给出的更直接建议：用你已经知道属于那个人的号码联系，而不是在可疑通道中继续完成一套猜真假游戏。你未必知道哪些个人信息已经被其他人获知，也不必靠自己识别每一种声音技术。把核实转到原先可信的联系方式，是改变信息来源；不断在同一次来电里追问，仍可能只得到同一个来源给出的回答。这个区别比单纯要求对方说得更像更有用。
:::

根据FTC的真实核实建议，把下列联系方式按来源分组。这是联系渠道练习，不是真实通话，也不会拨号。

::play{#a-familiar-voice-sort}

## 回到你原先就知道的联系渠道

FTC建议，联系那位被冒称的人核实；暂时联系不上，可以通过其他家人或朋友确认情况。不要把“暂时没接通”解释成可疑来电已经获得证明。

:::detail[核实的号码一定要和来电显示不同吗？]
重点不是数字是否不同，而是号码的依据是否独立于这次可疑请求。你从原先确认过的通讯录找出联系方式，和根据对方刚发来的一串数字拨打，是两种选择依据。即使两次看到的数字相同，也不要把声音与来电显示本身当成身份已经确认。按已知联系方式主动联系，并核实具体请求；暂时联系不上时，仍保留未确认状态。你不用懂仿声技术，先学会别让可疑来源自己证明自己。
:::

:::detail[这意味着所有紧急求助都应该被忽略吗？]
不是。核实是为了更清楚地帮助真正需要帮助的人，而不是否认一切求助。你可以先暂停被催促的行动，再联系已知对象确认。无法核实时，就保留未确认状态，不要把焦虑当作身份凭据。这里没有提供转账建议或处理真实紧急事件的完整流程，也不声称一个技巧能消除所有诈骗。你要练成的是一项明确动作：遇到要求立刻行动的身份声明，先通过独立渠道核对。
:::

## 自检

你收到一条催促立刻行动的消息，还附了一个新的联系方式。暂时拨不通原先知道的号码时，为什么仍不能把新消息当成已经核实？

## 一句话

**听起来是谁，不等于已经确认是谁；把核实带到独立的联系渠道。**

en.title: A Familiar Voice: Who Should You Contact Next?
en.content:
# A Familiar Voice: Who Should You Contact Next?

## A Question from a Real Regulatory Alert

A [2024 alert from the Federal Trade Commission](https://consumer.ftc.gov/consumer-alerts/2024/04/fighting-back-against-harmful-voice-cloning) discussed the risks of voice cloning being used for emergency requests from loved ones or demands from a boss, and provided verification advice. When you hear a familiar voice, which contact channel to use next is precisely the question this advice aims to address.

## Predict first
Where would you get the number for your next contact, and how would you avoid relying solely on the person you need to verify to prove their own identity?

Write down your thoughts first before reading on for the answer.

## Answer
Verify using contact information you have previously confirmed, rather than relying only on new details provided by the caller. Whom a voice sounds like and independently confirming whom you have actually reached are two different judgments.

## Following the New Information Provided by the Other Party

If the other party provides a number during a suspicious call and you dial it, that only proves you reached the person behind that number. In itself, that does not count as independent proof of identity.

:::detail[Why not test them first by asking about something only family would know?]
This follows the more direct advice from the FTC: reach out using a number you already know belongs to that person, rather than continuing a guessing game inside a suspicious channel. You may not know what personal details have already been learned by others, nor do you need to identify every voice technology yourself. Moving verification to a previously trusted contact method changes the source of information; continually asking questions during the same call can still leave you with answers coming from that same single source. That distinction is more useful than simply demanding that someone sound more convincing.
:::

Based on real verification advice from the FTC, group the following contact methods by their source. This is a contact-channel exercise, not a real phone call, and will not dial any numbers.

::play{#a-familiar-voice-sort}

## Returning to Contact Channels You Already Knew

The FTC advises contacting the person who is supposedly calling to verify; if you cannot reach them right away, you can check the situation with other family members or friends. Do not interpret "could not connect right away" as proof that the suspicious call was genuine.

:::detail[Does the verification number have to be different from the caller ID?]
The key point is not whether the digits are different, but whether the basis for the number is independent of this suspicious request. Looking up contact details in an address book you confirmed beforehand and dialing a string of numbers someone just sent you rely on two different foundations. Even if the numbers you see in both places are identical, do not treat the voice and the caller ID itself as confirmed identity. Proactively reach out using a known contact method and verify the specific request; if you cannot reach them right away, keep the status as unconfirmed. You do not need to understand voice-cloning technology—first learn not to let a suspicious source verify itself.
:::

:::detail[Does this mean all emergency pleas should be ignored?]
No. Verification is meant to help people who truly need assistance more clearly, not to reject every request for help. You can pause the pressured action first, and then contact a known party to confirm. When you cannot verify, keep the status as unconfirmed; do not treat anxiety as proof of identity. This lesson does not provide advice on money transfers or a complete procedure for handling real emergencies, nor does it claim that a single technique can eliminate all scams. What you want to practice is one clear action: when faced with a claim of identity demanding immediate action, check it first through an independent channel.
:::

## Check yourself
You receive a message urging immediate action, along with a new contact method. If you cannot temporarily get through on the number you already knew, why can you still not treat the new message as verified?

## In one sentence
**Whom someone sounds like is not the same as confirmed identity; take verification to an independent contact channel.**

lessons.content:
# 开始之前，你怎么知道怎样才算做好？

## 一份资料，两个不同的完成要求

[美国国会图书馆的2024年图书节页面](https://www.loc.gov/events/2024-national-book-festival)把现场活动、部分节目直播计划与会后录像安排分别说明。你想给没能到场的朋友做一份资料导览，朋友希望读完能继续找到节目资料，你先写下：“把这个活动介绍得有趣一点。”

这句话提出了期待，却还没有说明朋友读完以后应该能做什么。现在只编辑这份历史资料，不邀请别人参加已经结束的活动。

## 先猜一下

要判断导览是否做好，你会提前写下哪几项能直接检查的条件？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

先写朋友要完成的动作，再列必要信息：这是一份历史活动资料，直播与会后录像的范围不能混淆，原始入口能够找到。这样，你检查的是导览是否有用，而不只是文风是否讨喜。

## 把好不好，变成几个能对照的问题

你可以把请求改成：“给未能到场的读者写两句2024年图书节资料导览，保留部分直播与会后录像的区别，附原始页面。”

看初稿时，先看这几项在不在，再改语气。[请求写作指导](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt)中的清楚要求与相关背景，在这里变成了一份可实际使用的小清单。

:::detail[“有趣”和“好懂”就没有用了吗？]
它们有用，只是不能独自承担验收。例如你希望文字友好、短小，可以在必要信息之外继续提出这些偏好；但一句热情的“所有节目都能直播”即使很好读，也改变了原页面只说明部分直播的范围。先检查成品是否帮助读者完成任务，再调整它的表达，会让两类问题不再混在一起。你也不必给所有偏好打分：先选出错了就会误导读者的两三项，把其他地方留给编辑判断。
:::

两种工作阶段分别需要什么样的完成条件？先看你现在究竟要交什么。

::play{#define-done-weigh}

## 什么时候该反过来

你还没决定做文字导览还是图片卡时，可以先探索少量形式，不必提前规定每个字。等选定要交的东西，再把完成条件写清楚。

:::detail[为什么不一开始把条件写得越多越好？]
太早锁定细节，可能让你反复修改一个还没选好的方向。比如你只是在比较短信与资料卡，就可以先要各一份很短的结构建议；这时的完成条件是能比较两种形式，而不是已经拿到可发送的成稿。一旦选好导览，条件才收拢到目标读者、必须保留的信息和原始入口。每一轮仍有结束点，只是结束点随着任务阶段变化，而不是永远用“再好一点”让工作继续。
:::

:::detail[怎样避免检查清单也变成一份长作业？]
先问：这项若缺失，读者会做错什么？历史年份不清，可能把旧活动当成新活动；直播范围写错，可能误解观看方式；原始入口找不到，就难以继续查看。这三项已经足以支撑这次小导览。至于完整活动史、全部作者名单，并不是当前读者必须知道的内容。把检查条件限制在当前成品上，不是放弃严谨，而是让你知道这一轮何时能结束、还有哪些属于另一项任务。交给别人看时，也可以先问他能否找到下一步入口，而不是让他泛泛地评价喜不喜欢。这样得到的反馈更容易对应到你原来选定的任务。
:::

## 自检

原本的读者只想了解活动，现在想查当年能否远程参与。你的完成清单应当把哪一项信息提到前面？

## 一句话

**先说明成品要帮助谁做什么，完成条件才有可以核对的落点。**

en.title: Before You Begin, How Do You Know What Counts as Done?
en.content:
# Before You Begin, How Do You Know What Counts as Done?

## One Resource, Two Different Completion Requirements

The [Library of Congress 2024 National Book Festival page](https://www.loc.gov/events/2024-national-book-festival) describes scheduled in-person events, plans to livestream select programs, and post-event recordings separately. You want to make a resource guide for a friend who could not attend in person. Your friend hopes to use it to track down program materials afterward, so you initially write: "Make the introduction to this event a bit more engaging."

This statement expresses an expectation, but it does not yet clarify what your friend should be able to do after reading it. Right now, the task is only to compile this historical material, not to invite people to an event that has already ended.

## Predict first
To judge whether the guide is done well, which directly checkable criteria would you write down in advance?

Write down your judgment first, then scroll down to see the answer.

## Answer
First write down the action your friend needs to take, then list the essential information: this is historical event material, the scope of livestreams versus post-event recordings must not be confused, and the original entry point must be findable. That way, you are checking whether the guide is useful, not just whether the writing style is pleasing.

## Turning "Is It Good?" into Questions You Can Check Against

You can change the request to: "Write a two-sentence guide to the 2024 Book Festival materials for readers who could not attend, preserve the distinction between select livestreams and post-event recordings, and attach the original page."

When reviewing the first draft, check whether these items are present before refining the tone. The clear requirements and relevant context from the [prompt engineering best practices](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt) here become a practical, working checklist.

:::detail[Are "Engaging" and "Easy to Understand" No Longer Useful?]
They are useful; they just cannot carry the acceptance criteria alone. For example, if you want the writing to be friendly and concise, you can certainly add these preferences on top of the essential information. But an enthusiastic "Every program can be streamed live," no matter how easy to read, distorts the original page's scope, which only indicated livestreams for select programs. Checking first whether the finished piece helps readers complete their task, and only then polishing its expression, keeps the two kinds of questions from getting tangled together. You also do not need to score every preference: first pick out the two or three items that would mislead readers if wrong, and leave the rest to editorial judgment.
:::

What kind of completion criteria do the two working stages require? First look at what you actually need to deliver right now.

::play{#define-done-weigh}

## When to choose the other way

When you have not yet decided whether to create a text guide or an image card, you can explore a few formats first without specifying every word in advance. Once you have settled on what to deliver, write out the completion criteria clearly.

:::detail[Why not write down as many criteria as possible from the start?]
Locking down details too early can trap you in endless revisions on a direction you have not yet settled on. For instance, if you are simply comparing a text message with an info card, you can ask for a brief structural suggestion for each. The completion criterion at this stage is being able to compare the two formats, not having a ready-to-send final draft. Only after you choose the guide format do the criteria narrow down to the target audience, the essential information, and the original entry link. Every round still has a finish line; the finish line simply shifts with the project stage, rather than endlessly letting work drag on under the banner of "make it a little better."
:::

:::detail[How do you keep a checklist from turning into a long assignment?]
First ask: if this item is missing, what mistake will the reader make? An unclear event year might lead them to mistake an old event for a new one; a wrong livestream scope might mislead them about how to watch; and a missing link to the original source makes it hard to explore further. These three items are already enough to support this short guide. A complete history of the festival or a full roster of authors is not something current readers need to know. Limiting check criteria to the deliverable at hand is not abandoning rigor—it simply tells you when this round is finished and what belongs to a separate task. When sharing it with someone else, you can also ask directly whether they can find the next link, rather than asking for vague opinions on whether they like it. That way, the feedback you receive aligns much more cleanly with the task you originally set.
:::

## Check yourself
Originally, the reader only wanted to learn about the event, but now they want to check whether they could participate remotely back then. Which piece of information should your completion checklist move to the top?

## In one sentence
**First clarify who the deliverable helps and what they need to do; only then do completion criteria have a concrete anchor to check against.**

lessons.title: 改了五处以后，你知道哪一处起作用了吗？
lessons.content:
# 改了五处以后，你知道哪一处起作用了吗？

## 两个新版本，哪一步带来了变化？

你用[2024年图书节记录](https://www.loc.gov/events/2024-national-book-festival)写出两句给到场者看的历史导览。第二份请求改成面向未能到场的人，同时加了另一份材料，还要求写成五句话。两份文字不同，你想知道哪些差别与更换读者有关。

[Canvas的2024年发布介绍](https://openai.com/index/introducing-canvas/)展示了局部编辑与版本比较。这里用自己的编辑安排练习，不把它称为真实模型测试。

## 先猜一下

你会怎样安排下一轮，才能更清楚地检查更换读者这一项？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

保留同一份材料、相同的成品形式与长度，只改变目标读者。这样比较出来的差别，才更容易对应到这一个修改要求。

## 只改一项，先看它影响哪里

把原请求留在旁边，再复制一份，把“给到场的朋友”改成“给未能到场的朋友”。日期来源不变，仍写两句导览。你现在可以专门看：新稿是否把远程观看方式放到了更合适的位置。

这种对照能帮助你编辑请求，并不证明模型在任何时候都产生同样结果。

:::detail[为什么还要留原请求，而不只留新稿？]
只留新稿，你可能记不清先前同时改了什么。原请求、原材料和原稿放在一起，能帮助你还原这次比较的条件。若新稿增加了一个新日期，你可以直接查出它不是由更换读者所要求的变化，而是需要另行核对的问题。你要记录的是这次怎样安排任务，不必保存所有中间碎片；保留足以重新理解这一次修改的信息即可。涉及私人内容时，也不要为了留记录就把不需要的个人资料一并复制。
:::

这是根据同一份公开资料设计的编辑练习，不是已运行的模型结果。把两份请求之间的变化放到对应位置。

::play{#change-one-thing-sort}

## 一次改很多，也有适合的时机

已经确定要重做整份作品时，可以一次调整多项要求。但那是在追求一个更合适的新版本，不是在辨认哪一项改变起了作用。把这两个目标分清就行。

:::detail[只改一项，为什么也不能当成严格的效果证明？]
你没有控制模型版本、抽样过程以及每次运行的全部条件，因此一次文本比较不是普遍因果结论。这里的价值更小也更实际：你知道自己主动改了哪一项，能据此检查新稿是否朝目标变化。若结果不稳定，可以保留现象并重新核对，而不要宣称“换了这句话就一定提升多少”。[官方迭代建议](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt)鼓励清楚地调整请求；它并没有为你的这两份作品提供一个测量结果。
:::

:::detail[结果没有明显变化，要继续把要求写得更长吗？]
先看你期待的变化是否真的有机会出现在当前成品里。例如只问当年活动日期，不同读者也可能需要同一个答案；改读者后日期不变，是合理结果。若你要比较的是资料选择，就应让成品包含读者需要的参加或回看信息。检查的问题要与修改对象对应。看不出差别时，先判断任务是否足以显示差别，而不是把更多形容词堆进请求，再也分不清哪项要求真正重要。
:::

## 自检

你想比较“给原始资料”和“不给资料”的区别，却同时换了问题、模型和篇幅。怎样重新安排一个更容易看懂的比较？

## 一句话

**想看清一项修改的作用，就先保留其他相关条件不变。**

en.title: After Changing Five Things, Do You Know Which One Made the Difference?
en.content:
# After Changing Five Things, Do You Know Which One Made the Difference?

## Two New Versions: Which Step Brought the Change?

You used the [2024 National Book Festival record](https://www.loc.gov/events/2024-national-book-festival) to write a two-sentence historical guide for in-person attendees. In a second request, you switched the audience to people who could not attend in person, while also adding another source document and asking for five sentences. The two texts turned out differently, and you want to know which differences are related to changing the audience.

The [2024 launch announcement for Canvas](https://openai.com/index/introducing-canvas/) demonstrated targeted editing and version comparisons. Here, we use our own editing setup for practice without calling it an actual model test.

## Predict first
How would you set up the next round so you can more clearly isolate the effect of changing the audience?

Write down your judgment first before reading on to the answer.

## Answer
Keep the same source material, the same output format, and the same length, changing only the target audience. That way, any observed differences can be much more easily attributed to this single modification.

## Change Just One Thing to See What It Affects First

Keep the original request to the side and make a copy, changing "for friends attending in person" to "for friends unable to attend in person." Keep the date source the same, and still ask for a two-sentence guide. Now you can focus specifically on whether the new draft puts the remote viewing options in a more appropriate spot.

This kind of comparison helps you refine your requests; it does not prove that the model will produce the same outcome every time.

:::detail[Why keep the original request instead of just the new draft?]
If you only keep the new draft, you might not remember what else you changed at the same time. Keeping the original request, source material, and original draft together helps you reconstruct the conditions of the comparison. If the new draft introduces a new date, you can directly verify that it was not a change required by switching the audience, but rather an issue requiring separate verification. What you need to document is how the task was set up this time, without having to save every intermediate fragment; keep just enough information to reconstruct and understand this specific edit. When dealing with private content, do not copy unnecessary personal information just for the sake of keeping a record.
:::

This is an editing exercise designed around the same public source material, not live model output. Place the changes between the two requests into their matching positions.

::play{#change-one-thing-sort}

## There Is Also a Right Time to Change Many Things at Once

When you have already decided to redo the entire piece, you can adjust multiple requirements at once. But that is pursuing a more suitable new version, not identifying which change made the difference. Just keep those two goals distinct.

:::detail[Why can changing only one thing still not count as rigorous proof of effectiveness?]
You did not control the model version, the sampling process, or the full conditions of each run, so a single text comparison does not establish a universal causal conclusion. The value here is more modest and practical: you know which element you intentionally changed, and you can check whether the new draft moved toward your goal. If the results are inconsistent, you can note what happened and re-check, rather than claiming that "changing this sentence definitely improves performance by a set amount." The [official iteration advice](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt) encourages adjusting requests clearly; it does not provide a measured benchmark for your two drafts.
:::

:::detail[If there is no obvious change in the results, should you keep making the prompt longer?]
First see whether the change you expect actually has a chance to appear in the current output. For instance, if you only ask for the date of that year's event, different audiences might need the exact same answer; the date remaining unchanged after switching audiences is an expected outcome. If what you want to compare is source selection, your output should include the attendance or replay details that the audience needs. What you check should match what you modified. When you cannot see a difference, first determine whether the task itself can reveal that difference, rather than piling more adjectives into the prompt until you can no longer tell which requirement actually mattered.
:::

## Check yourself
You want to compare the difference between "providing source material" and "not providing source material," but at the same time you changed the question, the model, and the length. How would you rearrange this into a comparison that is easier to interpret?

## In one sentence
**To see the effect of a single change clearly, keep the other relevant conditions unchanged first.**

lessons.title: 它给了答案，你下次能自己做吗？
lessons.content:
# 它给了答案，你下次能自己做吗？

## 收到讲解以后，换一份材料还能做吗？

[Khan Academy在2023年介绍Khanmigo](https://blog.khanacademy.org/harnessing-ai-so-that-all-students-benefit-a-nonprofit-approach-for-equal-access/)时，展示了通过提问与提示引导学习的设计。[AERO的明确教学指南](https://www.edresearch.edu.au/guides-resources/practice-guides/explicit-instruction-practice-guide-full-publication)则讨论示范、练习与逐步减少帮助。它们不是这门课已经有效的证明。

现在你已经看过怎样检查活动公告的年份，接着拿到[2024年图书节的另一份真实材料](https://www.loc.gov/events/2024-national-book-festival)。你准备向助手要一点帮助，再自己找出活动日与开门时间。

## 先猜一下

你会请求什么样的帮助，才能留下一个真正由自己完成的检查动作？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

请它先指出应该看哪类信息，必要时示范一个字段，把另一个留给你自己查。完成后再回原文核对，而不是直接把它给的整份答案抄下来。

## 把帮助停在你能够接着做的位置

可以先请求：“指出页面上区分活动日期与当天时间的地方，不要替我填写；我先试着找一项，再请你核对。”如果你连字段意思都不懂，先看一个示范也合理。

在这份记录里，活动开始与开门是两个不同动作。自己找完后，再确认你没有把一个时间当成另一个。

:::detail[为什么不能把得到正确答案直接算成自己会了？]
答案在眼前时，你可能只是在辨认熟悉的字。换一份资料后，仍要知道去哪里找、每个日期跟哪个动作对应。这里用另一份真实公告，不是考你记住某一个历史数字，而是让你重新完成定位与核对。可以把自己查到的一项先写下来，再看原文说明；若查错了，就指出错在读者对象、日期身份还是字段混淆。你因此得到的是下一次能使用的改进方向，而不是只知道这一题有没有得分。
:::

:::detail[初次接触时，完整示范会不会让学习变差？]
不能这样一概而论。AERO指南中的示范与逐步撤去帮助，是为了让学习者从能够理解的步骤开始。你完全不知道怎样读一份材料时，先看一个字段怎样被查出来，可以提供起点；看过示范以后，再由你完成另一个字段，才有机会判断自己是否理解。问题不是能不能给答案，而是这一次帮助之后，还有哪一个合适的动作留给你做。不要把“独立学习”理解成不允许任何帮助。
:::

:::detail[怎样告诉助手你具体卡在哪儿？]
把已经做过的动作与卡住的一步放在一起。例如：“我找到了活动日期，但分不清8:30与9:00各指什么，请只帮我辨认旁边的动作词。”这比“我完全不会”更容易得到有针对性的帮助。得到解释后，换一个字段自己再找一次。你也可以把这条求助写在自己的笔记中：不是保存全部答案，而是保存怎样描述卡点。这样的记录在换课程或换工具时仍可能有用。例如已经分清8:30是开门、9:00是开始，就再用另一处时间检查自己能否指出对应动作。若仍然需要同一句提示，记下这一点，下一次先补练这个步骤；不要因为看过解释就把还没独立完成的部分跳过去。
:::

把几种求助安排放到对应阶段：第一次示范、留给自己尝试，或回到材料核对。

::play{#help-that-leaves-you-able-sort}

## 自检

你能复述刚才的解释，却无法在新公告里找出对应句子。下一次求助应该补哪一个动作，而不是只要求再讲一遍？

## 一句话

**好的帮助让你接得上下一步，不只是替你交出答案。**

en.title: If It Gave You the Answer, Can You Do It Yourself Next Time?
en.content:
# If It Gave You the Answer, Can You Do It Yourself Next Time?

## After Getting an Explanation, Can You Still Do It with Different Material?

When [Khan Academy introduced Khanmigo in 2023](https://blog.khanacademy.org/harnessing-ai-so-that-all-students-benefit-a-nonprofit-approach-for-equal-access/), it showcased designs that guide learning through questions and prompts. [AERO's explicit instruction practice guide](https://www.edresearch.edu.au/guides-resources/practice-guides/explicit-instruction-practice-guide-full-publication), on the other hand, discusses modeling, practice, and gradually reducing support. Neither is proof that this course is already effective.

Now that you have seen how to check the year on an event announcement, you receive [another real material from the 2024 National Book Festival](https://www.loc.gov/events/2024-national-book-festival). You prepare to ask an assistant for a bit of help, and then find the event date and opening time yourself.

## Predict first
What kind of help would you ask for so that you still leave a verification step to complete genuinely on your own?

Write down your judgment first before scrolling down to see the answer.

## Answer
Ask it to point out what kind of information to look at first, demonstrate one field if necessary, and leave another for you to look up yourself. Once finished, check back against the original text instead of simply copying down the entire answer it gave.

## Stop Help Where You Can Take Over

You can start by asking: "Point out where on the page the event date is distinguished from the times of the day, but don't fill them in for me; I'll try finding one item first, then ask you to check it." If you don't even understand what the fields mean, it is also reasonable to see a demonstration first.

In this record, event start and doors opening are two different actions. After finding them yourself, confirm that you haven't mistaken one time for the other.

:::detail[Why can't getting the right answer count directly as mastering it yourself?]
When the answer is right in front of you, you might only be recognizing familiar words. After switching to a different source, you still need to know where to look and which action each date corresponds to. Using another real announcement here is not to test whether you remember a specific historical number, but to have you carry out locating and verifying anew. You can write down one item you found first, then look at the original explanation; if you made a mistake, point out whether the error stems from the target audience, the identity of the date, or confusing fields. What you gain from this is a direction for improvement that you can use next time, rather than merely knowing whether you got points on this question.
:::

:::detail[When encountering something for the first time, does a full demonstration make learning worse?]
You cannot generalize like that. The modeling and gradual fading of support in the AERO guide are meant to let learners start from steps they can understand. When you have no idea how to read a source, seeing how one field is found can provide a starting point; after watching the demonstration, having you complete another field gives you a chance to judge whether you understand. The issue is not whether an answer can be given, but what suitable step is left for you to take after this assistance. Do not interpret "independent learning" as permitting no help whatsoever.
:::

:::detail[How do you tell an assistant specifically where you are stuck?]
Put the actions you have already taken together with the step where you are stuck. For example: "I found the event date, but I can't tell what 8:30 and 9:00 each refer to; please only help me identify the action words next to them." This is much more likely to get targeted help than saying "I don't know how to do this at all." After getting an explanation, switch to another field and search again yourself. You can also write this help request in your notes: not to save the entire answer, but to record how you described your sticking point. Such notes can still be useful when switching courses or tools. For instance, once you have distinguished that 8:30 is doors opening and 9:00 is the start, use another time to check whether you can point out the corresponding action. If you still need the same prompt, note it down, and practice this step first next time; do not skip over the part you haven't finished independently just because you read the explanation.
:::

Place several help arrangements into their corresponding stages: initial demonstration, leaving room to try on your own, or checking back against the material.

::play{#help-that-leaves-you-able-sort}

## Check yourself
You can recite the explanation just given, but you cannot find the corresponding sentence in a new announcement. What action should you add to your next help request, rather than just asking for it to be explained again?

## In one sentence
**Good help lets you take the next step, rather than just handing over the answer for you.**

lessons.title: 一段好用的请求，要整段背下来吗？
lessons.content:
# 一段好用的请求，要整段背下来吗？

## 一段旧请求，还带着上一场活动的信息

你保存了一段给[2024年图书节](https://www.loc.gov/events/2024-national-book-festival)写资料导览的请求。现在想用同一种写法整理[NASA的2023年观月夜公告](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/)。原来的请求里，不仅有“两句话、面向朋友”，还写着图书节年份和观看方式。

两份资料都真实，但不是同一项活动。

## 先猜一下

重新使用这段请求时，哪些部分值得保留，哪些必须替换或核对？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

保留读者、成品形式与检查方法，重新填写这次的材料和具体事实。不要让旧日期、旧地点或旧活动安排跟着写法一起被当成新任务的信息。

## 保存结构，不把一次的事实固定进去

把请求分成两部分就够了：“给哪类读者做什么，哪些信息必须核对”可以复用；“这次使用哪份原文，其中的日期和安排”要随任务更换。

[明确背景与要求的指导](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt)可以帮助你整理这种写法。你不需要背下一串固定话术。

:::detail[把所有具体内容都删掉，模板会不会太空？]
模板可以保留需要填写的提示，例如“原始材料：”“目标读者：”“最后交付：”“要核对的条件：”。空格提醒你做选择，而不是让助手猜。为了方便，也可以在模板旁保留一份旧例子，但要把它标成示例，并在使用时确认没有把示例中的年月日一起带进去。你要复用的是安排任务的方法，不是一段永远适用于所有人的成稿。对于每次都不同的事实，明确留一个需要核对的位置，比悄悄预填更安全。
:::

这次是在继续编辑同一份资料，还是已经换了任务？据此选择复用范围。

::play{#save-what-worked-weigh}

## 什么时候该反过来

只是继续编辑同一份历史资料时，可以保留它已经核对的事实与来源，不必每轮清空。只有任务或材料改变后，才逐项检查哪些旧内容不再适用。

:::detail[文件还能再次调用，说明里面的信息仍适用吗？]
不说明。[文件资料库说明](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001052)描述的是文件能够被保存与再使用，而不是文件内容永远适合新任务。你可以把一份材料找得很快，却仍要核对它属于哪一年、哪种用途、是否缺少当前任务的信息。继续改同一份历史卡片，可以保留相关文件；换成另一场活动，就要明确告诉助手使用新的来源。取用方便与适用范围，是两个不同的判断。
:::

:::detail[怎样给以后使用的自己留下一条有用说明？]
不要只写“这个提示很好用”。记下它适合什么成品、需要什么材料、用哪些条件检查。例如“适合把已核对的活动公告改成两句导览；每次更换年份、读者和来源；检查参加方式没有被改强”。这条说明比旧成稿更能帮助下一次工作，也会提示你何时不该直接套用。把模板借给别人时，还应去掉不属于公开材料的个人信息，不让一份方便的范本变成无意扩散资料的路径。模板里没有填好的位置也应当明显留空，不让下一位使用者误以为这些内容已经查过。
:::

## 自检

你要把自己的导览模板借给朋友。怎样让他看得出哪些位置要重新填写，而不误把旧活动日期当成已经核对？

## 一句话

**复用任务结构，每次重新确认属于这次任务的事实。**

en.title: Should You Memorize an Effective Prompt Word for Word?
en.content:
# Should You Memorize an Effective Prompt Word for Word?

## An Old Prompt Still Carrying Information from the Last Event

You saved a prompt used to write an information guide for the [2024 Book Festival](https://www.loc.gov/events/2024-national-book-festival). Now you want to use the same approach to organize [NASA's 2023 Observe the Moon Night announcement](https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/celebrate-international-observe-the-moon-night-at-nasas-goddard-space-flight-center/). The original prompt not only included "two sentences, written for friends," but also specified the book festival's year and how to watch.

Both materials are real, but they are not the same event.

## Predict first
When reusing this prompt, which parts are worth keeping, and which must be replaced or verified?

Write down your judgment first, then scroll down to see the answer.

## Answer
Keep the audience, deliverable format, and checking methods, and fill in this time's materials and specific facts anew. Do not let old dates, old locations, or old event schedules get treated as information for the new task just because they came along with the phrasing.

## Save the Structure, Don't Lock in One-Time Facts

It is enough to divide the prompt into two parts: "what to produce for which audience, and which information must be verified" can be reused; "which source text to use this time, and the dates and schedules within it" must change with each task.

[Guidance on clarifying context and requirements](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/10032626-prompt-engineering-best-practices-for-chatgpt) can help you organize this way of writing. You do not need to memorize a string of fixed phrasing.

:::detail[If all specific details are deleted, will the template be too empty?]
The template can keep prompts for fields that need to be filled in, such as "Source material:", "Target audience:", "Final deliverable:", and "Conditions to verify:". Blank spaces remind you to make choices rather than making the assistant guess. For convenience, you can also keep an old example beside the template, but label it clearly as an example and confirm during use that you haven't carried over the year, month, and day from it. What you want to reuse is the method for structuring the task, not a finished draft meant to apply to everyone forever. For facts that differ every time, clearly leaving a placeholder that needs verification is safer than quietly pre-filling it.
:::

Are you continuing to edit the same material, or have you already switched tasks? Choose the scope of reuse accordingly.

::play{#save-what-worked-weigh}

## When to choose the other way

When you are simply continuing to edit the same historical material, you can keep the facts and sources that have already been verified; you do not need to clear everything every round. Only after the task or material changes should you check item by item to see which old details are no longer applicable.

:::detail[Does the ability to access a file again mean the information inside is still applicable?]
It does not. The [documentation on file libraries](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001052) describes that files can be saved and reused, not that file content will remain suitable for new tasks forever. You can retrieve a source quickly, yet you still need to verify what year it belongs to, what purpose it serves, and whether it lacks information needed for the current task. Continuing to edit the same historical card allows you to keep the relevant files; switching to another event means you must explicitly tell the assistant to use new sources. Ease of access and scope of applicability are two different judgments.
:::

:::detail[How can you leave a useful note for your future self?]
Do not just write "This prompt works really well." Note what deliverables it suits, what materials it requires, and what conditions to check. For example: "Suitable for turning a verified event announcement into a two-sentence guide; update the year, audience, and source each time; verify that participation details haven't been exaggerated." This note will help future work far more than an old finished draft, and it will also alert you to when you shouldn't apply it directly. When lending a template to others, you should also remove personal information that is not part of public materials, preventing a convenient template from becoming a path for unintentionally leaking data. Any unfilled spots in the template should also be left visibly blank, so the next user does not mistakenly assume that content has already been checked.
:::

## Check yourself
You are lending your guide template to a friend. How can you make it obvious which fields need to be refilled, so they don't mistakenly treat old event dates as already verified?

## In one sentence
**Reuse the task structure, and reconfirm the facts belonging to this specific task every time.**

lessons.title: 昨天的方法失灵，是不是你突然不会了？
lessons.content:
# 昨天的方法失灵，是不是你突然不会了？

## 同一个工具名，也经历过不同阶段

[Google在2024年2月的说明](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-image-generation-issue/)记录了因图像问题暂停部分人物图像生成功能。[ChatGPT Search的2024年发布说明](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-search/)则记录了搜索能力加入产品。

一份旧教程所见的功能，未必就是你今天手里正在用的功能。这两次历史记录不是对当前状态的判断。

## 先猜一下

旧方法这次没有得到预期结果时，你会先核对哪些变化，再决定怎样修改请求？

先写下你的判断，再往下看答案。

## 答案

先核对当前工具提供什么能力、这次用了哪些材料和动作，再看原方法是否仍适用。不要先把变化解释成自己退步，也不要用更多肯定语气替代缺失的功能。

## 先查变化发生在哪一层

你原本需要带来源的查找，结果却只有一段没有链接的文字。先确认这次是否执行了搜索、当前功能是否可用，以及问题是否需要新材料，再考虑调整措辞。

历史发布记录能说明产品曾经怎样变化；现在的具体操作，要回到当前工具的说明或可观察结果。

:::detail[这是不是说教程永远追不上工具，所以不用学了？]
不必把所有知识都绑在某个按钮上。如何说明成品、选择材料、检查来源和区分写作与执行，是可以带到新工具里的判断。按钮位置与某个功能的开放范围，则要在使用时核对。你可以把笔记分成“我怎样安排任务”和“这个版本怎样完成动作”两部分；前者帮助你理解，后者提醒你何时需要更新。两份历史公告说明工具会变化，但不代表任何一条旧方法都失去价值。
:::

:::detail[一次没有链接，就能判断搜索功能坏了吗？]
不能光凭这一项现象断定原因。可能要先确认你提出的任务、是否选择或触发了相应动作，以及结果是否提供了可查看的来源。先记录自己看到了什么，再检查与你任务有关的状态；不要把“不知道为什么没出现”改写成“这个功能已经坏了”。若当前环境没有所需能力，可以换成手动提供已核对材料的任务，但要承认这是另一条路径，而不是把普通回答冒充一次搜索结果。
:::

:::detail[找到新说明后，旧记录需要全部删除吗？]
保留它当时适用的日期和范围即可。历史记录仍能解释为什么以前的操作与现在不同；误导来自把它当成当前唯一说明。你的课程笔记可以用一句“这项操作需要重新核对当前说明”指出变化，再保留仍然有效的任务结构。之后重新完成一项小任务，检查方法是否真的适用于新条件。更新一条链接或改一个按钮名称，只是维护记录，还不能代替这次实际检查。
:::

把遇到的变化放到先要核对的地方。先描述变化，不急着责怪自己或工具。

::play{#when-the-source-changes-sort}

## 自检

以前能做的图片处理现在没有出现。你如何把“我看到的现象”与“我猜测的原因”分开写，再查当前说明？

## 一句话

**方法失灵时先核对条件变化，再决定该改工具、材料还是请求。**

en.title: When Yesterday's Method Stops Working, Did You Suddenly Forget How?
en.content:
# When Yesterday's Method Stops Working, Did You Suddenly Forget How?

## The Same Tool Name Goes Through Different Stages

[Google's February 2024 note](https://blog.google/products-and-platforms/products/gemini/gemini-image-generation-issue/) recorded the pause on some image generation of people due to image issues. [The 2024 release notes for ChatGPT Search](https://openai.com/index/introducing-chatgpt-search/) recorded search capabilities being added to the product.

The features shown in an older tutorial are not necessarily the ones you are using in your hands today. Neither of these historical records is a judgment on the current state.

## Predict first
When an old method does not produce the expected result this time, which changes do you check first before deciding how to revise your request?

Write down your judgment first, then scroll down to see the answer.

## Answer
First check what capabilities the current tool provides and what materials and actions were used this time, then see whether the original method still applies. Do not start by explaining the change as your own regression, and do not use a more assertive tone to compensate for a missing feature.

## First check which layer the change occurred at

You originally needed a search with sources, but all you got was a paragraph of text without any links. First confirm whether a search was executed this time, whether the feature is currently available, and whether the question requires new materials before considering adjusting your phrasing.

Historical release notes show how a product changed in the past; for specific operations today, you must return to the current tool's documentation or observable results.

:::detail[Does this mean tutorials can never keep up with tools, so there is no point in learning?]
You don't need to tie all your knowledge to a specific button. How to describe the final deliverable, select materials, check sources, and distinguish writing from execution are judgments you can carry over to new tools. Button placements and the availability rollout of a specific feature, on the other hand, need to be checked when you use them. You can divide your notes into two parts: "how I structure tasks" and "how this version completes actions." The former helps you understand, while the latter reminds you when updates are needed. The two historical announcements show that tools change, but that does not mean every old method loses its value.
:::

:::detail[Can you conclude that the search feature is broken just because links were missing once?]
You cannot determine the cause based on this single symptom alone. You may need to first confirm the task you submitted, whether you selected or triggered the corresponding action, and whether the result provided viewable sources. Record what you actually observed first, then check the status relevant to your task; do not rewrite "I don't know why it didn't appear" as "this feature is broken." If the current environment lacks the needed capability, you can switch to a task where you manually provide verified materials, but acknowledge that this is an alternative path rather than pretending an ordinary response is a search result.
:::

:::detail[Once you find the new documentation, do all old records need to be deleted?]
Simply keep the dates and scope to which it applied at the time. Historical records can still explain why past operations differ from current ones; misinformation comes from treating them as the sole current instructions. Your course notes can point out the change with a single sentence like "This step requires verifying against current documentation," while retaining the task structures that remain valid. Afterwards, complete a small task again to check whether the method truly applies under the new conditions. Updating a link or renaming a button is just record maintenance; it cannot replace an actual check this time.
:::

Place the changes you encounter into what needs checking first. Describe the change first without rushing to blame yourself or the tool.

::play{#when-the-source-changes-sort}

## Check yourself
An image processing step you could previously do does not appear now. How do you write down "what I observed" and "what I guess caused it" separately before checking current documentation?

## In one sentence
**When a method stops working, check for changed conditions first before deciding whether to change the tool, the materials, or the request.**
